title: Session-aware retry defaults, rotating id keys, and stream checkpoint strategy across Python/TS/Go SDKs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers and internal teams report inconsistent retry behavior and surprising duplicate effects across language SDKs. Streaming reconnection semantics differ (some SDKs drop state, some attempt transparent resume), idempotency key generation is inconsistent (auto-generated opaque keys vs requiring user-supplied keys), and default backoff profiles are tuned differently per-language. This leads to: user-visible duplicate operations (billing/customer-impact), fractured debugging (different telemetry), and increased support/incident load.

Goal: Define a single cross-SDK resiliency baseline that: (1) provides sane session-aware retry/backoff defaults suitable for LLM inference and streaming usage, (2) standardizes idempotency key semantics and a safe rotation policy, and (3) defines a lightweight resume/checkpoint strategy for long-running/resumable streams. Deliverables: spec, per-language implementation, test matrix, docs, rollout plan and telemetry dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: A cross-SDK spec doc published describing the session-aware retry profile and rationale
Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs implement the same default retry profile with opt-out/config override
Idempotency key behavior consistent: SDKs accept user-provided keys, expose an opt-in deterministic auto-generator, and document rotation guidance
Streaming: SDKs implement a resume token checkpoint API and deterministic fallback to restart-with-offset when resume is not possible
Automated integration tests validate duplicate-suppression semantics for at-least-once delivery scenarios
Telemetry captures retry counts, idempotency-key usage, resume success rate, and cost impact; dashboards for SRE/Support created
Migration notes and deprecation plan communicated to customers and partner teams
proposed_solution: Define 'session-resilient' retry profile defaults tuned for inference workloads and interactive streams. Core policy (recommended defaults): max_attempts=5, initial_delay_ms=50, max_delay_ms=2000, multiplier=2.0, jitter=full; session_budget: 2500ms aggregated per-session before switching to conservative fallbacks. For unary requests require idempotency key for mutating operations; SDKs will accept a user-provided Idempotency-Key header. For non-mutating generation calls, SDKs will expose an opt-in auto_idempotency generator that produces V4-UUID + session fingerprint and exposes rotation API. For streaming: introduce lightweight resume tokens (opaque string) returned by the server at periodic checkpoints. SDKs will persist the latest token and attempt a resume on reconnect; if resume fails, fallback is restart-from-last-offset with a client-visible deduplication window (token_count/window) where server suppresses duplicates for X tokens. Provide lib-level helpers for Python/TS/Go to persist tokens safely and to surface resume failures for app-level reconciliation.
tech_notes: Backoff rationale: inference workloads are latency-sensitive but may hit transient GPU preemption or rate limits. Aggressive early retries (50ms -> 100ms) reduce perceived latency for quick transient errors; cap at 2s to avoid runaway retries on infra failures.
Session budget: measure per-session cumulative retry time to avoid repeated retries for the same user interaction (chat turn). SDKs will surface a 'session_budget_remaining' metric to telemetry.

Idempotency: recommend server-side canonicalization for keys (trim/normalize) and an idempotency TTL of 60 minutes for critical mutating ops. Auto-generated keys must include a visible prefix and version (e.g., redwood-auto-v1-<uuid>) to allow server-side compatibility and rotation.

Streaming resume: resume-token must be opaque. Server will return (resume_token, last_event_index). SDKs should store both. On reconnect SDK will call resume endpoint with token and desired start index; if mismatch, server returns RESUME_UNAVAILABLE and client falls back to restart and relies on dedupe window

Telemetry: emit 'retry.attempt', 'retry.policy', 'idempotency.provided', 'idempotency.auto', 'stream.resume.attempt', 'stream.resume.success' with dimensions for language, sdk_version, client_session_id, model
Safety: do not auto-generate idempotency keys for operations that mutate external customer state (billing, admin actions) unless user explicitly opts-in via an API flag
implementation_steps: Write and review cross-sdk spec (this ticket) and publish to /docs/sdk/retry-idempotency-blueprint
Design server-side compatibility hooks with API team (resume token format, idempotency TTL, normalization rules) - dependency ENG-91827
Implement core retry engine in internal shared module for each SDK (Python: common.retries module; TS: @redwood/sdk/retries; Go: retries package)
Add session_budget tracking and telemetry hooks in SDK runtime
Add idempotency API surface: request.option({ idempotencyKey: '...', autoIdempotency: true, idempotencyVersion: 'v1' })
Streaming: implement checkpoint persistence helpers and resume attempt flow; add unit/integration tests against mock resume endpoint
Create integration test matrix for network partitions, resume failures, duplicate suppression windows
Docs and migration guide: update quickstarts with examples for Python/TS/Go and clearly document opt-in flags

Rollout: feature-gate auto-idempotency by default disabled for customers; enable opt-in beta via account flag; after 6 weeks of telemetry consider enabling default for non-mutating generation endpoints
Post-release: dashboard QA, collect metrics, iterate on defaults based on observed resume success and duplicate rate
comments: 2025-02-16 - Aisha Patel: Triage notes: urgent after 3 tickets from support and one P0 incident involving duplicate model fine-tune triggers. Prioritize cross-language parity rather than language-specific micro-optimizations.
2025-02-18 - Maya Chen: Initial spec draft uploaded. Waiting on API team confirmation of resume token semantics. Reached out to @devops for server-side TTL concerns.

2025-02-21 - Lars Hakansson: Design review: suggested session_budget be adjustable per SDK config and exposed to end users. Also suggested conservative defaults for Go (serverless/backoff differences).

2025-02-25 - Maya Chen: Implemented Python prototype for retry engine and local unit tests. Observed that naive auto-idempotency produced collisions in test harness; switched to UUID v4 with prefix to reduce risk.

2025-02-28 - QA (Jamal Ortiz): Integration test added for stream resume success/failure. Found race when persistent token store throws transient IO errors; added retry on token persistence and metric 'token.store.retry'.
2025-03-03 - Docs (Rina Gomez): Drafted developer-facing docs and examples for Python/TS/Go; inclusion of migration guide and deprecation timeline requested.
2025-03-04 - Maya Chen: Open PRs for Python and TS. Go implementation PR in progress. Planning beta feature flag rollout to 20% of dev accounts next week for auto-idempotency opt-in.
